synopsis: Auto-GCAS takes control of F-16 and F-35 fighters and pulls them up when a ground collision is imminent [f15732]. Its development traces to the early 1980s, with F-16 fielding in 2014, illustrating a long development-to-deployment timeline [f1208]. F-35 integration followed in 2019; Lockheed Martin says agile development and reuse of F-16 work brought that integration seven years earlier than previously planned [f1443, f15735]. By that 2019 milestone, Lockheed Martin credited Auto-GCAS with saving eight F-16 pilots’ lives; the glossary repeats this credited outcome rather than supplying independent verification [f1444, f15736].

relations.note: Both report 2019 F-35 integration seven years early through reuse of F-16 work.
Both report eight F-16 pilots’ lives credited as saved by 2019.
F-35 integration extends the timeline beyond F-16 fielding in 2014.
Credited lives saved provide reported outcome evidence for the collision-avoidance function.
